probes.name: titan-bare-model-id
probes.feature: Embedding model accepted by CreateModelInvocationJob, bare foundation-model id
probes.detail: Accepted and ran to Completed in ~11 min: 100/100 success. 'modelInvocationType' omitted defaults to 'InvokeModel' (GetModelInvocationJob echoes it back). The service normalises 'modelId' to 'arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0'.

probes.name: titan-inference-profile-id
probes.feature: Inference profile id as modelId, as the chat path submits
probes.detail: An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the CreateModelInvocationJob operation: The provided model identifier is invalid. -- no 'us.' profile exists for this model; every batch-capable embedding model is ON_DEMAND only, so the bare id is the only valid form. ModelDetails.get_id(inference_profile=True) already falls back to the bare id when the model has no profile, so the chat path's call is safe here by accident, not by design.

probes.name: nova-multimodal-embeddings
probes.feature: Second family: Amazon Nova 2 Multimodal Embeddings, explicit InvokeModel
probes.detail: Accepted and ran to Completed in ~10 min: 98 success, 2 per-record errors (the two deliberately bad bodies). Same job shape as Titan.

probes.name: cohere-embed-english-v3
probes.feature: Cohere Embed v3 in a batch job
probes.detail: An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the CreateModelInvocationJob operation: Batch inference is not supported for model cohere.embed-english-v3 in region us-east-1.

probes.name: cohere-embed-v4
probes.feature: Cohere Embed v4 in a batch job
probes.detail: An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the CreateModelInvocationJob operation: Batch inference is not supported for the requested model -- note this wording does NOT name the model id, unlike the v3 refusal, so batches._refused_job() classifies it as a deployment failure (503 FeatureUnavailable) instead of an unsupported model (400).

probes.name: input-record-shape
probes.feature: What one embedding input record carries
probes.detail: Identical envelope to a chat record: {"recordId": <id>, "modelInput": <body>}, one JSON object per line, JSONL. 'modelInput' is the model's own InvokeModel body, not a Converse body: Titan {"inputText": "probe 0"}, Nova {"taskType": "SINGLE_EMBEDDING", "singleEmbeddingParams": {"embeddingPurpose": "GENERIC_INDEX", "text": {"value": "probe 0", "truncationMode": "END"}}} -- byte-for-byte the bodies stdapi/models/embedding/*.py already build.

probes.name: record-id-shape
probes.detail: Same rule as the chat path: 1-character, 11-character and 64-character ids all passed validation and came back verbatim, including '-', '_' and '.'. No 11-character constraint applies. The gateway's 64-character _CUSTOM_ID_MAX_LEN is safe as is.

probes.name: minimum-records-per-model
probes.detail: The same 100-record minimum applies (Service Quotas: 'Minimum number of records per batch inference job for Titan Text Embeddings V2' = 100, not adjustable; same for Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1 and Nova 2 Multimodal Embeddings V1). It is NOT enforced by CreateModelInvocationJob: a 99-record job was accepted, then reached status Failed ~5 min later with message 'Batch job <arn> contains less records (99) than the required minimum of: 100'. A short job writes no output file and no manifest at all -- only the empty out/ folder marker.

probes.name: converse-invocation-type
probes.detail: Accepted at submit, passed validation, was scheduled, ran, and reached status Completed -- with 100/100 error records and nothing usable. The per-record error is 'Failed to parse ConverseRequest for recordId: rec00004. Error: Unrecognized field "inputText" (class com.amazon.bedrock.ConverseRequest) ...'. Nothing on the submit path catches the mismatch, so an embedding job submitted with the chat path's hard-coded modelInvocationType='Converse' would look healthy and bill a whole batch window for zero results.

probes.name: output-file-layout
probes.detail: Unchanged from the chat path: s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/out/<jobId>/input.jsonl.out for the records and s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/out/<jobId>/manifest.json.out for the counters. One output line per input record, but NOT in input order (first ids back were rec00037, rec00020, rec00038), so results must be matched by recordId.

probes.name: output-record-shape
probes.feature: Where the vector is in a successful result line
probes.detail: {"recordId": <id>, "modelInput": <the request body, echoed back verbatim>, "modelOutput": <the model's own InvokeModel response>}. Titan modelOutput: {"embedding": [1024 floats], "embeddingsByType": {"float": [1024 floats]}, "inputTextTokenCount": 4} -- 'embeddingsByType' is present even though the request carried no 'embeddingTypes', which the synchronous path never sees. Nova modelOutput: {"embeddings": [{"embeddingType": "TEXT", "embedding": [3072 floats]}]}. The echoed 'modelInput' roughly doubles the output file, and for Nova media inputs it would echo the whole base64 payload.

probes.name: error-record-shape
probes.detail: Same shape batches._record_error() already reads: {"recordId": <id>, "modelInput": <echoed>, "error": {"errorCode": 400, "errorMessage": "Malformed input request: #/singleEmbeddingParams/text/value: expected minLength: 1, actual: 0, reformat your input and try again.", "expired": false, "retryable": false}}. 'errorCode' is an int, and the message quotes the model's own JSON-schema path -- never forwardable to a client. A failure raised before inference (the Converse-type job) carries only errorCode and errorMessage, with no 'expired'/'retryable' keys.

probes.name: manifest-shape
probes.feature: What the manifest reports for an embedding job
probes.detail: Same keys the chat path reads, plus media dimensions: {"totalRecordCount": 100, "processedRecordCount": 100, "successRecordCount": 100, "errorRecordCount": 0, "inputTokenCount": 397, "outputTokenCount": 0, "cacheReadInputTokenCount": 0, "cacheWriteInputTokenCount": 0, "cacheWrite1hInputTokenCount": 0, "inputAudioSecond": 0, "inputVideoSecond": 0, "inputStandardImageCount": 0, "inputDocumentImageCount": 0, "inputTextTokenCount": 0, "inputImageTokenCount": 0, "inputAudioTokenCount": 0, "inputVideoTokenCount": 0, "outputTextTokenCount": 0, "outputImageTokenCount": 0}. Embeddings bill on inputTokenCount only, outputTokenCount is 0. 'inputStandardImageCount' / 'inputAudioSecond' / 'inputVideoSecond' are the dimensions Nova multimodal embeddings are priced on (input_images, input_seconds) and no code reads them today. A job where every record failed writes a truncated manifest with the four counts and no token keys at all.

probes.name: mixing-models-or-record-kinds
probes.feature: One job carrying more than one model, or both embedding and chat records
probes.detail: Structurally impossible: 'modelId' and 'modelInvocationType' are job-level parameters, so one job runs exactly one model through exactly one endpoint. A Converse-shaped record smuggled into an InvokeModel embedding job is not caught at submit or validation -- it fails alone, as a per-record {"errorCode": 400, "errorMessage": "Malformed input request, reformat your input and try again."}, while the other 99 records succeed and the job still reports Completed. The gateway's existing one-job-per-model fan-out is therefore the right shape; only modelInvocationType has to be decided per job.

probes.name: batch-price-signal
probes.feature: Whether the price catalog's batch-tier signal matches runtime acceptance
probes.detail: It matches exactly, for embeddings as for chat. A batch-tier input_tokens price is published for amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 (0.00000001/token, half of standard), amazon.titan-embed-image-v1 and amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0 -- the three families that also carry batch Service Quotas and that the runtime accepts. No batch price and no batch quota exist for cohere.embed-english-v3, cohere.embed-multilingual-v3, cohere.embed-v4:0 or twelvelabs.marengo-embed-*, and the runtime refuses them. The catalogue still advertises batch=False for every embedding model, because _advertises_batch() requires 'TEXT' in output_modalities and an embedding model outputs 'EMBEDDING'.
